title: Independent penetration testing: existence, frequency and triggers
status_rationale: The Secure Construction Standard states that external penetration testing remains planned for Unbound. No independent test of any Echelon product has occurred; no firm has been engaged.
target_answer: An independent, accredited firm tests Unbound before any customer production data is loaded, at least every 12 months thereafter, and after material changes (new hosting, authentication redesign, new payment or custodian integration, new AI agent authority). Results are shared as a letter of attestation and, under NDA, the full report.
current_practice: No independent penetration test has been performed on Unbound or any Echelon product. One is planned but not scheduled.
intended_practice: Engage an accredited firm and complete an architecture-informed test before the first customer production data load.
provable: Nothing. No test, report or letter exists.
customer_statement: Unbound has not yet been independently penetration tested. An independent test is planned before customer production data is loaded; we will share the letter of attestation when available.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: When will the first independent test be scheduled, and with which budget?
Will testing precede any pilot with real donor data?

challenge.customer_intent: Independent evidence that a skilled attacker cannot readily compromise the service or other tenants' data.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Exploitable flaws in authentication, authorization, tenant isolation or financial workflows reach production.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: A time-boxed annual black-box test samples a point in time and depends heavily on tester skill; it often misses business-logic and multi-tenant flaws when testers lack architecture context, and is stale soon after release.
challenge.legally_required: Not for Echelon directly. NYDFS 500.5 and the FTC Safeguards Rule impose testing on covered financial institutions for their own systems; customers may extend expectations to vendors by contract.
challenge.contractually_required: Very commonly required by bank, wealth and enterprise customers as an annual independent test with summary or letter sharing.
challenge.historical_convention: Annual independent penetration test with letter of attestation is near-universal in vendor due diligence.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Structural rules can remove some classes (dynamic SQL, arbitrary JavaScript), focusing testers on authorization, logic and isolation, but cannot remove the need for independent adversarial evaluation.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Release gate requiring a current independent test covering the changed attack surface.
challenge.continuous_evidence: First-party adversarial test results per release (ECTL-PEN-006) between independent tests.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Architecture-informed independent testing (white-box, with threat models and structural claims) before launch and annually, plus change-triggered focused tests, plus continuous first-party adversarial tests labeled as such.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes: independent letter covers scope including structural-claim bypass objectives; first-party results are reproducible.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If continuous first-party testing were offered as a replacement for independent testing, institutional acceptance would be unlikely.
challenge.alternative_risks: Providing source and design material can anchor testers on documented assumptions; mitigate by including explicit objectives to find what the documentation does not describe.
supporting_arguments: The Secure Construction Standard already directs providing threat models and residual attack surfaces to external testers.
Business-logic flaws in grant and payment workflows are unlikely to be found black-box in a short engagement.

agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Likely, because it adds to rather than replaces the conventional independent test.'; institutional acceptance rating 'likely' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Cost is significant for a pre-revenue company.
Some customers specifically want black-box results to approximate an outside attacker.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.

title: Penetration test scope and methodology
status_rationale: The Secure Construction Standard directs providing testers with threat models, rules, evidence and residual attack surfaces without suppressing independent discovery; no scope has been defined.
target_answer: Scope covers external attack surface, web application and APIs, every user and administrative role, cross-tenant access attempts, business logic of grant approval, payee change, disbursement and fee workflows, the Limen browser boundary, Strata-backed data access, AI agent interfaces and tool authority, cloud configuration, assumed-breach internal perspective (compromised workforce, CI or agent credential) and environment segregation. Testing is architecture-informed with explicit objectives to bypass claimed structural controls. Methodology references OWASP WSTG, NIST SP 800-115 and PTES. Because this scope exceeds a conventional web application test, the first architecture-informed test is expected to cost more than a conventional test; cost levers in DD-COST-001 are hypotheses about cost per meaningful finding in later cycles. A white-box structural review of the L1 to L4 claims is scoped and priced separately, because a pen test cannot confirm them. Objectives also include WebAssembly guest tampering and boundary message replay, intra-tenant object access (donor to donor, advisor beyond delegation, partner to partner), deploy-path RLS removal, a poisoned agent instruction file and server-side document rendering.
intended_practice: Define scope and rules of engagement during firm selection.
customer_statement: Penetration test scope is planned to include tenant isolation, business-logic abuse, structural-control bypass and AI agent interfaces; no test has occurred. Echelon expects the first test to cost more than a conventional web application test because of this scope.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
residual_risks: Scope negotiated by the vendor may exclude weak areas; customers should review exclusions.

history.change: BL-018: stated that the first architecture-informed test is expected to cost more, with savings as later-cycle hypotheses; added objectives from the security review (OBJ-SKEPTIC-012, OBJ-PENTEST-002, OBJ-PENTEST-003, OBJ-PENTEST-006, OBJ-PENTEST-012, OBJ-PENTEST-016).

title: Tester qualifications, firm accreditation and independence
status_rationale: No firm has been selected; criteria are a recommendation of this research.
target_answer: Testing is performed by a firm independent of Echelon engineering, holding a recognized accreditation such as CREST (or NCSC CHECK where a UK customer requires it), with testers holding certifications such as OSCP or GIAC GPEN or GWAPT and demonstrable web and API testing experience; testers are under confidentiality, background-checked by their firm, and do not access real customer data. Firms or lead testers rotate at least every three engagements.
intended_practice: Apply these criteria in firm selection.
customer_statement: Tester selection criteria are planned, not yet applied.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Remediation and retest of penetration test findings
status_rationale: SOC2-016 requires recording findings, prioritization, fixes, exceptions and retest evidence for penetration testing programs; not implemented.
target_answer: Findings enter the vulnerability register under VUL SLAs; each fix adds a regression test or structural change preventing recurrence of the class; the testing firm retests and issues an updated letter showing remediation status.
customer_statement: Remediation and retest processes are planned; no findings exist because no test has occurred.

title: First-party continuous adversarial testing between independent tests
status_rationale: The Secure Construction Standard requires property-based, negative and adversarial tests of financial invariants; Tutela defines the security evidence model and requires that authors not be sole verifiers of critical changes (tutela@476dc682:docs/SECURITY-PROCESS.md). Neither is applied to a running Unbound system.
target_answer: Every release runs adversarial, negative and property-based tests of financial invariants, authorization and tenant isolation, authored independently of the code author, with results recorded as first-party evidence and made available for sampling by independent testers and auditors.
current_practice: Tutela tooling exists as a security engineering model; no Unbound code under test exists.
intended_practice: Apply Tutela and Praxis gates to Unbound once implementation begins.
customer_statement: First-party adversarial testing is planned as part of Unbound's construction; it is not independent testing and is not yet operating.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

challenge.customer_intent: Know that security does not degrade between annual tests.
challenge.adverse_outcome: New features introduce flaws that persist until the next annual test.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Annual tests leave up to a year of untested change.
challenge.contractually_required: Rarely; customers ask but seldom require continuous testing.
challenge.historical_convention: Annual testing; some vendors add continuous automated attack surface scanning or bounties.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Invariants enforced at persistence and transaction boundaries reduce what adversarial tests must cover.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Adversarial and property-based tests run in CI as release gates.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Continuous first-party adversarial testing of invariants plus change-triggered independent tests.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Partially; first-party results can be sampled by the independent tester or SOC auditor.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Unknown; unvalidated. The prior agent judgment is kept in supporting_arguments.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Tests authored by the same agent or person who wrote the code; tests that only confirm intended behavior.
challenge.alternative_risks: Risk of presenting first-party evidence as if independent, which the Secure Construction Standard prohibits.
supporting_arguments: Property-based tests can explore input spaces far beyond manual testing.
agent judgment: customer acceptance likelihood 'Uncertain as a substitute; likely as a supplement.'; institutional acceptance rating 'uncertain' (unvalidated, no cited source).
opposing_arguments: Institutions value independence over volume; first-party evidence is discounted.
AI-generated tests may share blind spots with AI-generated code.

Institutional acceptance is unvalidated: no buyer, auditor, regulator or insurer evidence or cited source supports an acceptance rating (DD-VAL-ADV-001, DD-VAL-ADV-002). Treat any rating as agent judgment until target-customer conversations or a sourced document support it.
